environment: RC receiver powered through the VTX, so the RC link was live

observations: Image identity matched the USB gate: ELF 6bdcd149..., binary 16f6e8ed..., clean tree at a921ffe.
Boot was stationary and disarmed. config-show read the baseline before and after the run.
Operator confirmed OSD VBAT and cell voltage consistent with a multimeter across the pack at 6 cells, 4.18 V per cell, closing the missing-cell-voltage half of the 2026-07-28 report.
Motors were stopped at boot and did not respond to stick movement while disarmed.
Arming succeeded five times, each through the guarded stop dwell and four-motor eRPM qualification before SYSTEM ARMED. No motor started before that transition.
Arming aborted correctly when throttle was raised during the attempt: 'Arming aborted: throttle exceeds 65'.

Deliberate RC loss while armed stopped the motors immediately: DShot to [0, 0, 0, 0], eRPM zero in the next report. All five 'RC link invalidated by frame timeout' events were operator-initiated. No automatic rearm followed recovery; a fresh ARM-low then ARM-high was needed.
Operator verified motor reaction as expected on roll and pitch, correction opposing the imposed motion, full-stick bounds reached, deadband commanding zero.

The logical-to-physical motor path is byte-identical to pre-conversion 18521d5: MOTOR_OUTPUT_MAP [3, 4, 2, 1], the Quad X mixer, the ferrowasp-core frame conventions, and every Foxeer pin and timer. The conversion cannot have moved a motor, and no wiring or airframe change intervened.

Battery current read a constant 0.1 A including at four motors turning 6300..7700 eRPM. Conversion is centiamps = adc_mv * 10000 / 70 / 10, so 0.1 A implies a raw PC1 reading near 1 mV, the noise floor. The defect is upstream of the scale-70 change this candidate adopted, which therefore could not have fixed the 2026-07-28 zero-current report.

The ESC telemetry manager latched a fault at 207999 ms after one response timeout for physical output 4 (logical M4) at request 10131: one miss in 10132, zero CRC failures. Earlier disarms, including the first RC-loss stop, reached zero eRPM unfaulted, so the miss was not systematic.

Both later arming attempts then aborted on 'ESC idle telemetry qualification timed out', correctly fail-closed. The second followed a battery reconnect, but the latch was already set 100 s earlier, so this run does not independently demonstrate the carried-forward ESC-only power-cycle bug.
After the latch, per-motor eRPM repeated frozen values while DShot commanded [0, 0, 0, 0]: the stale-telemetry item already tracked, not turning motors. Operator confirmed motors stopped.
Blackbox wrote 1398 pages, zero dropped records, zero write faults. Capture: boot 4, flight 8, pages 17182..18560.

No 'UART4 RX free-buffer pool exhausted on IDLE' warning occurred with the VTX connected and powered, against two in the earlier USB-only run with UART4 floating. The deferred pre-conversion A/B is no longer needed for this symptom.

The first storage-CLI command after each USB port open was rejected once with 'ERR invalid command; type help' and succeeded on retry. CommandParser in crates/ferrowasp-tasks/src/flash_storage.rs accumulates a line with no reset across port open, so a stray byte corrupts the first line and the error clears the buffer. Byte-identical to pre-conversion: pre-existing, cosmetic.
limitations: No oscilloscope or logic analyzer: DShot pulse width, jitter, and complementary-output margin were not measured; motor stop is evidenced by the firmware's DShot reports, not at the pins.
Battery current magnitude is unusable, so no loaded-current cross-check was possible.

Motor identity came from the roll and pitch differential response plus the unchanged output map, not the capped per-motor identification procedure, which needs a bench-only selector image that step 1 forbids.
This board has no reset button, so boot-with-ARM-high was exercised as a USB power cycle only.
Yaw was exercised within the stick and correction checks but not logged per motor pair.
stop_conditions_triggered: Abnormal current: battery current read a constant 0.1 A with four motors turning, an implausible loaded reading under step 2 of the procedure.
Telemetry fault: the ESC telemetry manager latched faulted after a response timeout for logical M4, and the two subsequent arming attempts aborted on idle telemetry qualification.
